newsitem.title: HONG KONG: GOLF-DEVENPORT ECLIPSES STAR NAMES IN ALFRED DUNHILL MASTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DEVENPORT ECLIPSES STAR NAMES IN ALFRED DUNHILL MASTERS.

text.p: Unheralded New Zealander Paul Devenport fired an eight-under-par 63 to eclipse big names like Colin Montgomerie and Ernie Els as he took the first-round lead in the Alfred Dunhill Masters on Thursday.
Devenport, 30, shot eight birdies to lead by one shot from South Korean Kang Wook-soon in the event co-sanctioned by the Australasian and Asian PGA Tours.
Devenport splits his tournament schedule between Australia and Canada but has yet to win an event while Kang has triumphed twice this year to lead the Asian Order of Merit standings.

Montgomerie, the Scot crowned king of the European circuit for the fourth consecutive year in Valderrama last week, recovered from an opening double bogey to record a two-under-par 69 while Els, the triple World Matchplay champion, shot 71.
"I did not make any mistakes today - it was a good solid round and I'm delighted with it," said Devenport, whose 63 was one off the course record held by Nick Faldo of England.

Montgomerie blamed jet-lag and the stifling heat for his stuttering round while Els, who arrived on Wednesday after his sixth place finish in the rain-delayed U.S. Tour Championship, said that he failed to find his rhythm.
"I just could not get going," said Els. "It was just one of those days."
German Bernhard Langer, a winner on this Fanling course at the 1991 Hong Kong Open, began with a five-under 66 while troubled Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros had a level-par 71.
This season Langer failed to win a European Tour event for the first time in 17 years and is seeking a triumph to help him "turn the corner." He again used a long-handed broomstick putter.
Ballesteros reiterated that he is finding it hard to concentrate on his golf game because of commitments as captain of Europe's Ryder Cup team for next year.
